Per-head decay -8 on every token of a 1024-token prefill: over a 16-token chunk the within-chunk decay prefix reaches exp(-128), below the f32 subnormal floor, so a chunked formulation that divides keys by exp(prefix) produces Inf/NaN while the recurrence itself applies a finite exp(-8) per token. Bounded Q/K/V, beta 0.5, no past state.

skipGpu.reason: The chunked prefill decomposition materializes a normalized key as k divided by exp(the within-chunk decay prefix). A sustained decay of -8 drives that prefix to -128 over a 16-token chunk, so the exponential underflows to zero and the division returns Inf/NaN, while every pairwise term the decomposition actually needs carries the bounded ratio exp(p_t - p_s) <= 1. The serial route applies a finite exp(-8) per token and stays finite. Fixing this needs the chunk operands re-anchored to a per-chunk pivot, with the entry-state terms kept in their absolute form.

provenance.notes: Decay -4 keeps each 16-token chunk prefix at -64, within the float32 exponent range, so `k / exp(prefix)` remains finite. It is the finite-prefix control for `gated_delta_chunked_strong_decay_prefix_underflow`.
